title: Improving Training Attendance
situation: An executive education unit is seeing attendance fall below target in its flagship professional development programme. Participants cite scheduling conflicts, last-minute communication, and unclear reporting lines as reasons for non-attendance.
dilemma: The programme lead must decide between sending individual reminders, enforcing a mandatory-attendance policy, or redesigning the schedule based on participant feedback.
tasks: Draft a communication to re-engage participants; summarise feedback trends; create an action plan; prepare a risk note on mandatory attendance
risks: Privacy if personal attendance data is used; tone insensitivity; overgeneralisation from limited feedback; policy overreach
debrief: What should a human reviewer check before this communication is circulated? What risks does a mandatory attendance policy introduce?
role_options: Programme Lead; Training Coordinator; Senior Manager; HR Representative
decision_paths: Send targeted reminder emails; Redesign schedule after survey; Enforce attendance policy with escalation; Commission a root-cause study first
expected_output: Executive brief with options; stakeholder email draft; attendance improvement action plan

title: Executive Decision with Incomplete Data
situation: A department head must submit a resource allocation recommendation within 48 hours but has incomplete data on staff availability, budget approvals, and project timelines.
dilemma: Proceed with best available information and flag gaps; request extension; delegate to a sub-team; use scenario planning to cover uncertainty.
tasks: Prepare a decision memo under uncertainty; identify missing information; create three scenarios; draft a request for an extension if needed
risks: Hallucination risk if AI fills data gaps with invented figures; overconfidence in partial analysis; missing accountability trail
debrief: How should a decision memo signal uncertainty to the reviewer? At what point is incomplete data too risky to proceed?
role_options: Department Head; Resource Manager; Senior Analyst; Governance Officer
decision_paths: Submit with clearly flagged data gaps; Request 48-hour extension; Delegate with documented assumptions; Use scenario memo with three options
expected_output: Decision memo with flagged uncertainties; scenario planning note; extension request draft

title: Process Improvement in Administration
situation: An administrative operations team spends significant time on manual reporting, fragmented communication, and inconsistent document formatting across units.
dilemma: The operations manager must identify which tasks could be supported by AI without introducing security or quality risks, and prepare a pilot plan for leadership approval.
tasks: Map current workflow; identify AI-suitable tasks; create a risk register; draft a pilot proposal with safeguards
risks: Data handling if documents contain personal information; over-automation without review; inconsistent output quality; dependency risk
debrief: Which tasks should remain fully manual? What governance structure should oversee the pilot?
role_options: Operations Manager; Process Improvement Lead; IT Coordinator; Compliance Officer
decision_paths: Automate formatting and template generation only; Extend to summary and brief generation with review; Defer until governance policy is confirmed; Run a controlled two-week pilot first
expected_output: Process improvement note; risk register; pilot proposal draft

title: Stakeholder Communication Challenge
situation: A cross-functional project team has received contradictory feedback from three different stakeholder groups. Leadership wants a consolidated communication note that acknowledges all views without creating further confusion.
dilemma: The project lead must decide whether to address all concerns in one message, send targeted communications to each group, or convene a clarification meeting first.
tasks: Draft a consolidated stakeholder communication; summarise conflicting feedback; propose a resolution approach; flag risks of each option
risks: Tone misalignment for different audiences; selective representation of feedback; escalation if concerns are not acknowledged; perception of favouritism
debrief: How do you ensure all stakeholder groups feel heard without creating conflicting commitments?
role_options: Project Lead; Communications Specialist; Department Head; External Relations Officer
decision_paths: Send one consolidated message acknowledging all views; Send targeted notes to each group; Convene a briefing session before any written communication; Escalate to senior leadership for guidance
expected_output: Stakeholder communication draft; feedback summary; communication risk note

title: AI Adoption Resistance
situation: A team has been introduced to AI-assisted drafting tools but adoption is low. Some members cite trust concerns, others raise workload issues, and a few believe manual methods are more reliable for their specific work.
dilemma: The manager must address resistance without mandating adoption in a way that undermines trust. A communication and change-management approach is needed.
tasks: Create an adoption communication strategy; draft a reassurance note; identify root causes of resistance; design a low-pressure pilot
risks: Mandate without buy-in causing further resistance; privacy concerns if usage is tracked; perception that AI replaces roles
debrief: What combination of reassurance, training, and demonstration is most likely to build genuine adoption?
role_options: Manager; Change Management Lead; HR Representative; Training Coordinator
decision_paths: Run an optional demonstration session first; Survey team members to surface specific concerns; Mandate a limited pilot with feedback collection; Share success examples from comparable teams
expected_output: Change management communication; adoption plan; reassurance note

title: Healthcare Appointment Workflow
situation: A health services management team is reviewing its patient appointment scheduling process. Average wait times have increased and administrative staff are managing competing requests from multiple departments manually.
dilemma: The operations lead must evaluate whether AI-assisted scheduling support can reduce wait times without compromising patient data safety or decision authority.
tasks: Map the current scheduling workflow; identify AI-suitable steps; assess data sensitivity; draft a responsible-use note for leadership approval
risks: Patient data privacy; over-reliance on AI scheduling; edge cases requiring human judgement; liability if AI misroutes urgent appointments
debrief: Which scheduling tasks are safe for AI assistance and which must remain under human control at all times?
role_options: Operations Lead; Healthcare Administrator; Data Governance Officer; Clinical Services Manager
decision_paths: Use AI for non-clinical scheduling support only; Restrict AI to template generation and reminders; Conduct a three-month pilot with audit trail; Defer pending a full privacy impact assessment
expected_output: Responsible-use note; workflow map; risk register for healthcare AI

title: Recruitment Screening Ethics
situation: An HR team is considering using AI to pre-screen applications for a professional development cohort based on stated criteria such as experience level and leadership history.
dilemma: The HR lead must evaluate the ethical implications of automated screening and decide how to communicate the approach to applicants and internal stakeholders.
tasks: Identify ethical risks of AI-assisted screening; draft a transparency note for applicants; create a human-oversight checklist; propose safeguards
risks: Bias in screening criteria; lack of transparency with applicants; appeal process gaps; legal compliance if adverse outcomes occur
debrief: What minimum human oversight is needed at each stage of an AI-assisted recruitment process?
role_options: HR Lead; Compliance Officer; Programme Director; Diversity and Inclusion Representative
decision_paths: Use AI to flag incomplete applications only; Use AI as a first-pass filter with human review of all borderline cases; Avoid AI screening entirely for this cohort; Pilot AI screening for one criterion only
expected_output: Ethics note; transparency communication; human-oversight checklist

title: Reporting Efficiency Improvement
situation: A programme management team currently produces weekly status reports manually, resulting in inconsistent formats, delayed submission, and low readability for senior reviewers.
dilemma: The programme manager must propose a standardised AI-assisted reporting workflow that reduces preparation time without compromising accuracy or accountability.
tasks: Design a standardised report template; identify AI-suitable report sections; create a review checklist; draft a proposal for leadership approval
risks: Template rigidity reducing nuance; AI generating generic observations from limited input; accountability gaps if authorship is unclear
debrief: How would you ensure that AI-assisted reports still reflect genuine human analysis and institutional judgement?
role_options: Programme Manager; Operations Analyst; Senior Reviewer; Team Lead
decision_paths: Standardise template and use AI only for formatting; Use AI to generate first draft with mandatory human review; Automate data aggregation and manual narrative; Pilot with one report type for six weeks
expected_output: Standardised report template; review checklist; workflow proposal

title: Cross-Functional Coordination Challenge
situation: Multiple departments are working towards the same programme deadline but operating independently with different update formats, inconsistent priority rankings, and limited shared visibility on risks.
dilemma: The coordination lead must design a communication and information-sharing approach that creates alignment without adding administrative burden.
tasks: Map the coordination gaps; propose a shared update format; draft a coordination communication; identify the minimum viable oversight mechanism
risks: Information overload if too many meetings are added; format fatigue if standards are too rigid; siloing if only one channel is used
debrief: What is the minimum structure needed to create genuine coordination without creating compliance overhead?
role_options: Coordination Lead; Programme Manager; Department Representative; Senior Oversight Officer
decision_paths: Introduce a weekly one-page update template shared via a common platform; Establish a fortnightly coordination call with a standard agenda; Assign a single coordination point of contact per department; Use a shared risk log as the primary alignment mechanism
expected_output: Coordination communication; shared update template; risk log framework

title: Service Quality Improvement
situation: A public-facing service unit has received a cluster of complaints about unclear information, inconsistent responses across channels, and long resolution times. Leadership wants an improvement plan within two weeks.
dilemma: The service manager must determine whether the issue is primarily one of communication quality, process design, staff training, or information accuracy.
tasks: Categorise complaint themes; create an improvement priority list; draft a response framework for common complaint types; prepare a management brief
risks: Overgeneralising from complaint clusters; identifying symptoms rather than root causes; communication that appears defensive rather than responsive
debrief: What would a human reviewer check before an AI-assisted response framework was sent to service staff?
role_options: Service Manager; Quality Improvement Lead; Communications Officer; Operations Head
decision_paths: Commission a root-cause analysis first; Implement a standardised response framework immediately; Run a short training session on common complaint themes; Create a tiered escalation protocol for complex complaints
expected_output: Complaint analysis note; response framework draft; management brief
